sources.ins:
Three parts: recruit → train → manage.
Ramp a new rep in about 14 days before live leads; decide early when to cut.
Manage with huddles, 1-on-1s, reviewing call recordings ("game tape") and the numbers.
Principle from their handbook: advanced = never skipping the basics.
sources.cb: Not for now: you are Stage 1 with no sales team. Learn it; apply after the first 3 paying agencies.

sources.overlap: Not in your library. Its ideas were later generalised in the $100M books, so much will overlap; the gym-specific tactics do not transfer directly.
sources.cb: Do not copy gym tactics. Principles that may transfer to agencies: front-loaded results in the first weeks, retention through early wins. Hypotheses, to be tested.
sources.note: No official companion workbook for Gym Launch Secrets could be verified. Third-party "summaries" exist and are not used as sources.

sources.ins:
Buyers describe their pain in plain repeated phrases; sellers write in their own words.
They had AI read only the calls that bought, collected the buyers' phrases, and put them in ads, VSL and the first lines of the script.
Pain (what they want to stop) motivates more than the promise.
Action: a one-page "Why people buy" doc from 20–30 buyer calls.
sources.cb: Adaptation for Caregiver Bench (hypothesis): you have no buyers yet, so start from owners' own words in your call notes ("caregivers don't show", "I'm covering shifts myself"); use them in the opener. Test: owner-conversation rate before vs after.
